result.title: When Does Spatial Cooperation Help? Contamination Regimes in Decentralized Online Spectrum Anomaly Learning
result.comment: 7 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. Extended version of a paper accepted to IEEE MILCOM 2026, Workshop S4: Smart Systems for Signal Intelligence, Sensing, and Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations, including the proofs omitted from the conference version
result.summary: Learning-based spectrum monitors adapt online to benign propagation changes, but persistent rogue transmissions can gradually become incorporated into the learned background. Spatially distributed receivers provide additional evidence for detecting such anomalies, while decentralized model mixing can also spread contamination to receivers with clean measurements. We study this tradeoff using a decentralized online learner with sample gating and model sharing. We show that, without defenses, contamination propagation is governed by the occupancy rate and is independent of cross-receiver correlation. In contrast, the benefit of spatial fusion depends strongly on correlation and the detector operating point, so cooperation can either improve or degrade detection. We also show that fragmented transmissions can evade gating based on temporally smoothed statistics. Combining smoothed and per-sample gating substantially improves robustness to such intermittent contamination.

AI.brief_summary: 研究去中心化在线频谱异常学习中的污染传播与空间协作权衡：带样本门控与模型共享的在线学习器表明，无防护时污染扩散由占用率决定而与接收器间相关性无关，融合收益则强烈依赖相关性，并提出结合平滑与逐样本门控以抵抗间歇性污染。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「证据融合收益取决于相关性、共享状态会把污染扩散到干净来源」的分析，可能为 LVR 中多视图/多裁剪视觉证据的融合收益判断与门控式证据筛选提供概念线索，可供核查是否可迁移。
